name: TV Detox
cost: Free (MIT). The AI route needs Claude Code or Codex. The scripts alone need only adb
works_with: Claude Code or Codex, on Android TV and Google TV sets
short: Your coding agent strips bloatware and ads off a slow Android TV over Wi-Fi, then installs a tiny ad-free home screen.
what: You turn on developer mode on the TV and paste one prompt into Claude Code or Codex on a laptop on the same network. The agent connects to the TV, lists every app in plain English, asks before each change, turns apps off instead of deleting them and keeps an undo list. Then it installs a small home screen with your apps, your HDMI inputs and a clock, which uses about 30 MB of RAM.
who: Anyone with a slow Android TV or Google TV, including many Sony, TCL, Hisense, Philips and Xiaomi sets, Chromecast with Google TV and Nvidia Shield. It doesn't work on Roku, Samsung (Tizen) or LG (webOS). Fire TV gets the cleanup but keeps Amazon's home screen.
needs: An Android TV or Google TV. Tested on Android TV 9, 11 and 12, and Google TV 14
A laptop on the same network as the TV
Claude Code or Codex on that laptop. Without AI you only need `adb` (`brew install android-platform-tools` on a Mac)

steps.title: Turn on developer mode
steps.text: On the TV, go to Settings, Device Preferences, About and press Build 7 times. Then turn on USB debugging in Developer options. Read the README's notes and warnings first.

steps.title: Open your agent
steps.text: Start Claude Code or Codex on the laptop. The laptop and TV must be on the same Wi-Fi.

steps.title: Paste the prompt
steps.text: Copy the numbered prompt from the README and fill in your TV's brand and model and the apps you use. The agent asks you before every change.

steps.title: Turn debugging off
steps.text: When it's done, turn off USB debugging in Developer options, plus Network or Wireless debugging if you turned them on.

steps.title: Or skip the AI
steps.text: Download the repo and run `sh install.sh <TV_IP>` to install just the home screen. `sh candidates.sh <TV_IP>` lists every app with a verdict and changes nothing.

steps.title: Undo it
steps.text: This brings back the TV's own home screen. To undo the cleanup too, ask your agent to reverse everything on its list.

try.label: From the README
try.where: Claude Code or Codex on your laptop
try.text: "Help me clean up my Android TV and make it faster. My TV is a <brand and model>." followed by the rest of the README's numbered prompt.

watch: This turns off system apps, at your own risk. A few TVs got stuck at the logo or kept restarting. The README explains how to recover.
On Google TV and Chromecast with Google TV, don't turn off Google TV's own home screen. Some needed a factory reset. `install.sh` leaves it on by default.
While debugging is on, other devices on your network can ask to control the TV. Turn it off once you're done.
On an OLED TV, keep the screensaver on to avoid burn-in.
Some remote buttons, like the YouTube button on some Google TVs, can stop working.
The Claude app and claude.ai can't reach your TV, because they run on Anthropic's servers. You need an agent running on your laptop.
